reason: The myoblasts must fuse to form the multinucleated muscle cells described in the chapter.
expectation: The aligned myoblasts will join into multinucleated muscle fibres or their precursors.

effect: Fusion produced a mature multinucleated fibre with actin grip sites still covered, suggesting calcium is needed next.
reaction: The distinction between one fibre and many fused cells is useful.
reason: The calcium pulse spreads around the filaments and should enable the fibre to pull.
expectation: Calcium will expose actin's grip sites and allow myosin to pull the filaments.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites and enabled filament sliding; the fibre now needs to become ready again.
reaction: The distinction between sliding filaments and shortening filaments is helpful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes should remove calcium from around the filaments and help reset the fibre.
expectation: ATP-powered pumps will return calcium to storage, allowing the fibre to relax and become ready for another signal.

effect: ATP-powered calcium removal stopped pulling and completed the fibre-cycle goal; the remaining task is to build and attach both muscles.
reaction: The outside pull needed to lengthen the relaxed fibre is a useful detail.
reason: The empty biceps sheaths are meant to contain muscle fibres.
expectation: The fibre will be incorporated into the biceps muscle construction.

effect: The attempted biceps assembly revealed that fibres first need connective tissue to form fascicles; there are enough bundles for both muscles.
reaction: The intermediate connective layers clarify how fibres are grouped.
reason: The fascicles can now fill the empty biceps sheaths and connect to their tendons.
expectation: The fascicles will form a biceps muscle within its sheaths and tendons.

effect: The fascicles filled the biceps heads, and connective tissue links their force to the tendons. Fascicles remain for the triceps.
reaction: The force-transfer inset makes the tendon connection clearer.
reason: The remaining fascicles should fill the triceps sheaths just as they filled the biceps sheaths.
expectation: The fascicles will form a triceps muscle with tendons ready to attach to the skeleton.
